case_name: B. Chandra Manikyamma v. B. Sudarsana Rao Alias Saleem Mohammed

parties.respondent_defendant: A-1 and others (husband and family members)

facts_of_case: The wife filed a complaint against her husband and his family members for bigamy. The trial court convicted the accused and sentenced them to imprisonment and fine. The complainant now files an appeal.

legal_principles.principle: Admissions made by parties can be taken into account to prove a fact, including the fact of marriage.
legal_principles.held: The admissions made by the parties also can be taken into account to prove that they are husband and wife.

legal_principles.principle: The conduct of parties, supported by oral and documentary evidence, can be taken into consideration to prove a fact.
legal_principles.held: The conduct of the parties, supported by oral and documentary evidence with regard to the admissions also can be taken into consideration with regard to the proof of the first marriage.

legal_principles.principle: A valid first marriage can be proved by the orders passed by competent courts, even if the ceremonies are not strictly followed.
legal_principles.held: If we read Section 50 of the Evidence Act coupled with the orders passed by the two competent courts, it can be held that there is a valid first marriage between Neelaveni and A-l.

outcome.final_order: The final court order set aside the convictions and sentences awarded by the trial court.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for judicial separation
preparing a response to a divorce petition
advising on the implications of bigamy in a matrimonial dispute
